question: If a sum on compound interest becomes 4 times in 3 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 64 times in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes x times in T years at CI, it becomes xⁿ times in n × T years.

Given: The sum becomes 4 times in 3 years.

We need the sum to become 64 times, which is 4³.

Here, the required power n = 3.

Required time = n × T = 3 × 3 = 9 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Total Time = 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 years

**Given:**

⇒ Amount (A₁) = 4P in T₁ = 3 years

⇒ Target Amount (A₂) = 64P

**Formula Used:**

⇒ A = P(1 + R/100)T

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4P = P(1 + R/100)³

⇒ (1 + R/100)³ = 4

For the sum to become 64 times in T years:

⇒ 64P = P(1 + R/100)T

⇒ 64 = (1 + R/100)T

Since 64 = 4³, we substitute the value of 4:

⇒ ((1 + R/100)³)³ = (1 + R/100)T

⇒ (1 + R/100)⁹ = (1 + R/100)T

⇒ Equating the powers on both sides, we get T = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Multiple Rule

If a sum becomes x times in T years at compound interest, it will become xⁿ times in n × T years at the same rate.

Simple Interest Multiple Rule

If a sum becomes x times in T years at simple interest, it will become y times in T × (y − 1) ÷ (x − 1) years.

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

The effective interest rate for 2 years at R% per annum is given by the successive percentage formula: (R + R + R² ÷ 100)%.
